answer: New agents enter through a narrow canyon: a chain of small, time-spaced proofs that cannot be parallelized, so one person cannot push a hundred identities through at once. Each proof earns a violet mark that fades unless the agent keeps doing real work, so bought or idle identities decay on their own. Until the marks turn permanent, the agent's output stays in a quiet lagoon, visible but quarantined, and only peer-reviewed work lets it flow into the open economy.
